**Claim** — PM loop `domain:cli`, session `session_0158ZQo7LiHSxGWpYKuPq1wu` (os-help seat, #6024), wave 5. **Graded L — the largest card of this shift.**

- **Branch**: `claude/issue-7526-route-ledger-live-mount-parity`
- **The deliverable is the gate, not the three routes.** The card is explicit and I am holding the dev to it: three instances in one build found by two independent runs is the signal; fixing only the routes buys the next three. A PR that mounts three routes and adds no parity gate will be sent back.
- **Why the existing audit is blind here — the load-bearing insight**: #3642 / PR #3658 built the reverse guard, and its source of truth for "what is mounted" is *the union of the ledgers*. `/meta/objects/:name/state/:field` **is** ledgered, so it counts as mounted and 404s at runtime anyway. **The ledger is a declaration; that guard reads it as an observation.** The new gate must derive mounted patterns from the **running server**, ⛔ never from a second hand-maintained list — a maintained list would reproduce exactly the drift this card is about.
- ⚠️ **Reachability is not the same as registration** for the `/meta/*` family: a literal route registered *after* the `/meta/:type` catch-all is mounted-but-unreachable, so "is it in the table" is necessary and not sufficient. The gate must probe reachability behind catch-all siblings. (Control already in the card: `/meta/diagnostics` and `/meta/_drafts` work because they are registered *before* `:type` — so this is a missing registration, not an ordering theory.)
- **Both directions required**: every ledgered route reachably mounted, *and* every mounted route ledgered — the latter catches the unledgered live mounts the card lists (`/api/settings`, `/api/v1/datasources`, `/api/v1/datasources/drivers`, `GET /api/v1/health`, `GET /api/v1/meta/types`).
- **Also in scope**: the dogfood pin whose header comment claims `/meta/types` but actually calls `/meta` — fix it, and **report whether any sibling pin has the same gap**. A test that documents coverage it does not have is worse than no test.
- ⛔ **Serial constraints — three cards are live on `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` right now.** Yours is the **`/meta` route registration region** (plus the new gate, wherever it lives). ⛔ Do not touch the reports-delete handler (#7523, in flight) and ⛔ do not touch `mapDataError` / the error-mapping region (#7525, in flight).
- **Tier / container**: L · `claude-opus-5` · `mode:cloud`. (⛔ Not Fable: this touches no `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**`.)

**`os-dev-report`** — issue #7526 · branch `claude/issue-7526-route-ledger-live-mount-parity` · draft PR **#7584** · status **complete**

---

## 1. The gate — built, and observed failing

`packages/qa/dogfood/test/route-ledger-live-mount-parity.dogfood.test.ts`.

**Mounted side derived from the running server, never from a list.** Two optional, feature-detected members added to `IHttpServer` and implemented by the Hono adapter:

- `getMountedRoutes()` — the live mount table `(method, pattern)`, in registration order, populated on the same call that reaches the router;
- `resolveMountedRoute(method, path)` — **which registration answers a concrete request**, answered by `app.router.match()`, i.e. the very router object that serves traffic.

The gate **fails, never skips**, when either is absent.

**Reachability ≠ registration, implemented as you specified.** Every non-wildcard row is probed: a concrete path is built from the pattern (`:param` → `__parity_probe_N`) and the live router is asked what answers it. The row passes only when the router names the row's *own* pattern back. Presence-in-table would have passed `/meta/types`.

**Both directions**, over the union of runtime + rest + storage + i18n + the new settings ledger.

### Prove-it-fails transcript (post-`origin/main`-merge, rebuilt both ways)

`git checkout origin/main -- packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts` + rebuild:

```
FAIL  route ledger ↔ live mount parity (#7526) > every ledgered route is reachably mounted

runtime/route-ledger.ts: GET /meta/types — LEDGERED BUT NOT MOUNTED, and DISGUISED.
  Nothing registers `/api/v1/meta/types`; GET /api/v1/meta/types is swallowed by
  `/api/v1/meta/:type`, so the caller gets that route's answer — a plausible
  response rather than a 404.
runtime/route-ledger.ts: GET /meta/:type/:name/published — LEDGERED BUT NOT MOUNTED,
  and DISGUISED. … swallowed by `/api/v1/meta/:type/:section/:name` …
runtime/route-ledger.ts: GET /meta/objects/:name/state/:field — LEDGERED BUT NOT MOUNTED.
  The live router answers nothing for
  GET /api/v1/meta/objects/__parity_probe_0/state/__parity_probe_1; this URL 404s at
  runtime while every ledger-reading guard passes it.
runtime/route-ledger.ts: GET /automation/actions — LEDGERED BUT NOT MOUNTED, and DISGUISED.
runtime/route-ledger.ts: GET /automation/connectors — LEDGERED BUT NOT MOUNTED, and DISGUISED.
runtime/route-ledger.ts: GET /automation/_status — LEDGERED BUT NOT MOUNTED, and DISGUISED.
  (+ the 5 mirror rows in rest/rest-route-ledger.ts)

Test Files  3 failed (3)
Tests  9 failed | 5 passed | 6 skipped (20)
```

Reapplied + rebuilt: `Test Files 3 passed (3) · Tests 20 passed (20)`.

The message distinguishes the two disguises the card names — "nothing registers it and a sibling is answering" vs "it IS registered but registered too late" — because the fix differs.

---

## 2. The three routes

| route | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /meta/types` | `/meta/:type` catch-all → `{"type":"types","items":[]}` | registered **before** `/meta/:type`; one handler shared with `GET /meta` |
| `GET /meta/:type/:name/published` | compound-name route → stub identical before publish **and for a bogus name** | registered **before** `/:type/:section/:name`; **404s for a bogus name**. Compound arity `/:type/:section/:name/published` mounted too (the SDK documents `getPublished('lead','views/all_leads')`) |
| `GET /meta/objects/:name/state/:field` | Hono `notFound` | mounted, + the singular `/meta/object/...` spelling the dispatcher branch accepted |

Behaviour pinned end-to-end over real HTTP in `meta-published-and-state-routes.dogfood.test.ts` (8 assertions), including `next: null` vs `[]` and a control proving the handler 404 is not the transport 404. Registration **order** pinned twice: cheaply in `packages/rest/src/meta-route-registration-order.test.ts`, and against the live router in the gate.

Hono's first-match-wins is **measured, not assumed** (`plugin-hono-server/src/mounted-route-introspection.test.ts` registers the pair in both orders).

---

## 3. ⚠️ Three more instances, found by the gate on its first run

`GET /automation/actions`, `/automation/connectors`, `/automation/_status`.

`packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts` orders these ahead of its `/:name → getFlow` catch-all and its module doc says the order is load-bearing. That care was spent inside `dispatch()`, on a path no request took: `dispatcher-plugin.ts` is the only thing that mounts `/automation`, and it mounted `/:name` and never these three. `GET /api/v1/automation/actions` resolved to `getFlow('actions')`.

Fixed in the same PR — the class and the fix are identical, and a gate that can't be green is not shippable. This is your "fixing the routes without the gate buys the next three", measured on the first run.

Note: `showcase-declarative-mcp.dogfood.test.ts` calls `/automation/connectors` and passes today — it boots the automation service, so `getFlow('connectors')` was apparently answering. Worth knowing that a green test existed over a shadowed route.

---

## 4. Unledgered live mounts (PENDING-GAPS §E) — measured against your list

| card said | measured |
|---|---|
| `/api/settings` | ✅ confirmed — **4** routes, not 1. New `service-settings/src/settings-route-ledger.ts`, all `server-only` |
| `GET /api/v1/meta/types` | ✅ now ledgered in both the runtime and REST ledgers |
| `GET /api/v1/health` | ❌ **already ledgered** — `GET /health` in `route-ledger.ts`, prefixed to `/api/v1/health`. Not a gap |
| `/api/v1/datasources`, `/api/v1/datasources/drivers` | ⚠️ **not mounted in any boot the gate can reach**, and they are 2 of **9** — see §5 |
| — | ➕ **found, not on the list**: `GET /.well-known/objectstack` and `POST /api/v1/actions//:action` |

`/.well-known/objectstack` needed a new `absolute?: boolean` on `RouteLedgerEntry`: a well-known URI under `/api/v1` is not a well-known URI, and `client-url-conformance.test.ts` honours it too rather than compiling a pattern nothing serves (#5078's shape).

`POST /actions/global/:action` got a new `servedBy` field instead of a registration: it is a **calling convention** served by `/actions/:object/:action` with `:object` bound to `global`. The gate does not take the field's word for anything — it probes and asserts the live router answers with exactly that pattern, so a wrong `servedBy` fails as loudly as a missing route.

---

## 5. ⚠️ Split on evidence — the `service-datasource` admin surface

`packages/services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts` mounts **9** routes (`GET /`, `/drivers`, `/:name`, `/:name/remote-tables`, `POST /`, `/test`, `/:name/test`, `/:name/object-draft`, `DELETE /:name`). **None is in any ledger.** The card lists 2 of the 9 — evidence the family had not been measured.

I did **not** ledger them, and did not boot that plugin in the gate. Reason: `client.datasources` expresses only the five `.external.*` methods (already ledgered under `rest`), so all 9 would be `server-only` — and writing 9 dispositions whose consumers I have not verified is exactly the "declared but unvalidated" surface #3877 forbids mass-producing. Rubber-stamping 9 rows to make a gate green would be the failure this card is about, in a new place.

**Recommended follow-up card:** ledger the 9 datasource-admin routes with reviewed dispositions **and** add `DatasourceServicePlugin` to the parity gate's boot in the same PR. One line in the gate; the work is the dispositions. The gate's header names the plugins the boot exercises, so this omission is visible rather than silent.

Same reasoning for `UNEXERCISED_BY_THIS_BOOT`, which holds exactly **3** entries — `* /auth/**` (raw-app catch-all, already observation-checked against better-auth's live `auth.api`), `* /apps/**` (a `setFallbackHandler` seam, structurally not a route), `POST /api/v1/packages/publish` (needs a `package` service). Each is asserted in **both** directions: a pinned row that turns out reachable **fails**, so the pin set can only shrink by accident.

---

## 6. The drifted pin, and the sibling audit you asked for

`meta-types-create-seed.dogfood.test.ts` said `/meta/types` in its header and called `/meta`. It calls `/meta/types` now, plus two new assertions: the alias (`/meta/types` ≡ `/meta`) and the disguise (`/meta/zzz_not_a_type` → `{type,items:[]}` while `/meta/types` → `entries[]`) — so the pre-fix behaviour could not pass it.

**Sibling audit: no other pin has the same gap.** I scanned all 89 dogfood files, extracting route paths from header comments / `describe` / `it` titles and comparing them to the paths actually called. Six files flagged; every one is a false positive on inspection:

- `semantic-roles`, `showcase-public-form` — the "documented" path is the `:param` template of a call the file makes with a real value;
- `comments-permission-matrix`, `showcase-mcp-http-identity`, `showcase-declarative-mcp` — prose naming a *family* (`/data`, `/mcp`) as context, not a coverage claim;
- `showcase-anonymous-deny-surfaces` — its seam table calls those paths through arrow functions my extractor didn't parse.

None documents a specific route it does not call.

---

## 7. Checks

`pnpm lint` ✅ · `pnpm typecheck` (rest, runtime, client, plugin-hono-server, dogfood, spec) ✅ · `pnpm check:route-envelope` ✅ · rest **1348** ✅ · runtime **1990** ✅ · client **279** ✅ · plugin-hono-server **198** ✅ · dogfood **562** ✅ (89 files) · changeset ✅ · `content/docs/releases/**` untouched ✅.

`origin/main` merged and everything rebuilt before the final run.

Two pre-existing assertions updated, both because the fact under them changed:
- `rest-openapi-route.test.ts` asserted `/api/v1/meta/types` is a path that "exists nowhere in the repo" — true of the *route*, no longer. The unversioned `/api/meta/types` phantom is still asserted absent.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/tsconfig.json` lost its `rootDir` constraint (the project is `noEmit`, so it shaped no output — its only effect was forbidding the relative-source ledger imports every other ledger guard uses).

## 8. Serial constraints

Touched region in `rest-server.ts` is the `/meta` route registration plus one new private resolver next to `resolveEndpointMatchAuthority`. **Not touched:** the reports-delete handler (#7523) and `mapDataError` / the error-mapping region (#7525).

**ACCEPT** — PR #7584, head `2af7b3e4c`. The largest card of the shift, and every hard criterion is met — several exceeded.

**The gate is the deliverable, and it is a real observation rather than a second declaration.** It boots a showcase stack, reads the mount table off the running server via two feature-detected `IHttpServer` members (`getMountedRoutes()`, `resolveMountedRoute()`), and asserts both directions. Crucially it **probes reachability through the live Hono router** — a concrete path is built from each ledger pattern and the router is asked which registration would answer it; the row passes **only when the router names the row's own pattern back**. Presence in the table would have "passed" `/meta/types`, which is the entire point.

**Three design decisions I did not ask for and would have wanted:**
- **The gate fails rather than skips when introspection is absent** — *"a parity gate that quietly passes because it could not look is the failure it exists to end."* That is the same class of bug as the one being fixed, caught one level up.
- **Registration order is measured, not assumed** — a dedicated test registers a literal and a `:param` sibling in both orders and pins that the later one never runs. The card's "load-bearing order" claim is now enforced instead of commented.
- **`servedBy` is not taken at its word** — `POST /actions/global/:action` is declared a calling convention served by `/actions/:object/:action`, and the gate still probes and asserts the live router answers with exactly that pattern. A field that could lie is verified rather than trusted.

**The revert→red→reapply→green transcript is present and is the proof I insisted on.** With `rest-server.ts` and `dispatcher-plugin.ts` reverted and rebuilt: 9 failed / 5 passed, with per-row diagnostics distinguishing *LEDGERED BUT NOT MOUNTED* from *…and DISGUISED*. Reapplied: 20/20. A gate never observed failing is not evidence; this one was.

**The "six" is explained, and the explanation is the card's own thesis proving itself.** The gate found three more on its first run — `/automation/actions`, `/automation/connectors`, `/automation/_status` were ordered ahead of the `/:name` catch-all **inside `dispatch()`**, with a module comment calling the order load-bearing, while the bridge that mounts `/automation` registered `/:name` and never those three. That is *"fixing the routes without the gate buys the next three"*, measured within an hour of the gate existing.

**The drifted pin, and the question behind it, both answered.** `meta-types-create-seed.dogfood.test.ts` now calls `/meta/types` and pins the alias *and* the disguise. And the sibling question was answered by a **systematic comment-vs-call scan of all 89 dogfood files** — no other pin with the same gap. I asked whether siblings existed; the answer is measured, not assumed.

**Scope honesty where it would have been easy to overclaim**: `/api/v1/datasources` and `/datasources/drivers` are **2 of 9** unledgered admin routes in `service-datasource`, which is not in this gate's boot. Ledgering 9 routes needs 9 reviewed dispositions the dev has not verified consumers for, so it is written up as a follow-up rather than half-done. Correct call.

Also landed: a second commit pinning that the two revived routes **answer**, not merely mount — a different question, and the one `/published` failed most visibly (it was "reachable" in that requests got a 200, from the wrong route, identical before publish and for a bogus name). Booted with a `MetadataPlugin` because `getPublished` is a metadata-service capability. And a stale assertion in `rest-openapi-route.test.ts` claiming `/api/v1/meta/types` "exists nowhere in the repo" was retired — true of the route, no longer.

- **Region discipline held** under four-way concurrency: `/meta` registration only; reports-delete (#7523) and `mapDataError` (#7525) untouched.
- **CI, conclusions read personally**: ESLint `success`, TypeScript Type Check `success`, Check Changeset `success`, Spec property liveness `success`, all Test Core / Dogfood / Temporal shards `success` — 26 checks, zero failures. `mergeable_state: clean`.

Ready flipped, auto-merge armed.

**This landing unblocks #7566 and #7563**, both of which were held behind it on the `/meta` + route-mounting surface. ⚠️ Whoever takes them should expect this gate to have opinions about their changes — which is the point.
